contradictions: The hold_tsk_owned commit says HMS=4 latched 'as soon as OP is stopping' gives the TSK hold on every stop. The parent and hms_latch_fix reach the same latched HMS=4 state 0.40 s later, so the change only swaps that 0.4 s window. Yet hold_tsk_owned drives fault on hills and the parent drives so far did not. So either the window matters to the ESP, or something else differs between the drives.

The d861e6b comment says the latch stops the 4->1->3->4 cycling. On this car (ESP_21 bit 53 never set) the replay shows it is a no-op: f30a396 and d861e6b give identical frames in every real scenario. The parent still cycles 4->1->4 at standstill on every stop<->pid flip.

The d861e6b evidence that the 'ESP tolerates long steady HMS=4' is 60 frames (1.2 s) on 5.6%. The parent's longest logged hill holds are 11.4 s at +2.4% and 2.9 s at -4.8%. On the +11.2% stop the driver braked at +0.34 s. There is no log of the parent holding a hill of 5% or more for longer than 3 s.

The MQBStandstillManager docstring says at_standstill = standstill OR vEgo < 0.5, and that the ESP engages hold within 2-5 frames of HMS=1. The code uses vEgo < 1.0, and the logs show bit 53 never set.

A comment says CC.longActive is used for HMS so that brakePressed cannot force HMS=0. But the long_active value the manager returns is never used afterwards, and the ACC_07 HMS is computed without acc_enabled gating. As a result HMS=1 is sent for one frame with OP long already off on a brake disengage.

contradictions: Meaning of ESP_33 bit 28. The user brief (T line 3), 02_history.md item 2 and 04/05 (study) call it 'ESP standstill hold ACTIVE'. Route 333 shows bit 28 = 1 at 4.9 m/s while the TSK brakes, = 0 whenever TSK torque is 0 (HMS 1, launch), and = 1 again when torque returns under HMS 4. It therefore follows the ESP carrying out the TSK brake-torque request, probably Soll-Radbremsmoment. 'SRBM accumulation' in 89a239f/f30a396/6bacc4d and the '152 s SRBM hold' therefore probably mean TSK-braking frames at standstill, not an ESP hold budget being used up.

Bit 53 hold confirmation. 89a239f says the 'ESP engages hold within 2-5 frames on flat/hill'. 8613283 says 'always False in 45k+ frames'. The user brief says the hold handshake 'works -- it does'. Routes 332/333 show it never set on 7 stops from -4.8% to +11.2%. d861e6b describes HMS 3 cycles on 0000022b, but this code only sends HMS 3 when bit 53 = 1. A possible reconciliation: the '2-5 frames' figure matches bit 63's observed 0.03-0.04 s response, not bit 53.

Steady HMS 4 at standstill. 89a239f says TIMEOUT->HMS 4 'prevents SRBM accumulation'. f30a396 says 'permanent HMS=4 -> SRBM'. 6bacc4d says 'HMS=4 accumulates SRBM ... trips TSK'. d861e6b says it is 'tolerated 60+ frames'. Routes 332/333 held 3-26 s with no fault. hold_tsk_owned faulted at standstill in 2/2 drives. One explanation fits all of these but is unproven: HMS 4 is tolerated only after an ESP stopping procedure (bit 63) has run, as RJ describes.

9439ecc's own justification says the TSK holds '20-26 s with no faults ... more than any road grade needs, so no grade special-casing'. That branch then faulted at standstill on hills in routes 337 and 338. The 20-26 s evidence came from flat stops on 1478030, where a bit-63 episode came before the latch; hold_tsk_owned removed that episode.

TSK grade compensation. 9439ecc says the torque 'does not appear grade-compensated'. Data: flat 141-143 raw (and still ramping), +2.4% median 97 (lower even than full compensation predicts, about -15 raw), -4.8% 121 (looks like flat; compensation would add about +30). mk7_hold_trace's expectation model leaves out creep and the ramp: flat torque is 1.5-1.8x m*a*r. Inconclusive.

Study claims (01_hold_chain.md 1.3, 03_external.md, 04 H5) that this build's latched split, ACC_06 Anhalten plus ACC_07 HMS 4, is 'the opposite of RJ', and that a TSK left in stopping zeroes its torque. RJ's code forces ACC_06 to starting only while it acquires the grant (bit 63 on, or < 9.5 km/h before the latch), and after that ACC_06 follows lcs (Anhalten at standstill) with ACC_07 START, which is the same split. Route 333 shows the TSK holding 116-143 raw with ACC_06 Anhalten = 1 and HMS 4. H5 does not hold on flat stops.

Study hypothesis H4 assumed that the TSK grade-compensates -1.2 to about 0.13 m/s2 of brake at 11%. The actual 11.2% rollback happened with TSK torque at 0 because HMS 1 started at standstill (plan lag, H8/H1). Torque was not weak under HMS 4.

HMS 0 as the safe resting state. 6bacc4d/8613283 call it 'fault-free (11,461 grade frames)'. That data came from srbm_grade_hold_fix, where engine torque held the car with the accel floor gated on noisy aEgo. 89a239f says HMS 4/0 at standstill gave 'zero hold frames' and rollback. MEB notes say HALTEN->KEINE faults into park.
92b7fb4 calls SRBM accumulation the way hill hold engages ('prevent hill hold from engaging via SRBM accumulation'). 89a239f, 6bacc4d and d861e6b treat SRBM accumulation as the path to a TSK fault.

The '812 HMS switches per 1000 grade-standstill frames, mostly 0<->4' figure (user brief, after d861e6b) does not match route 332. Per source, route 332 had about 0 per 1000; with all sources mixed it had 62 per 1000. Mixing explains part of the effect but not its size, and no trace from the hms_latch_fix era has been redone.

Code comments versus code on HEAD: the comments say at_standstill uses vEgo < 0.5 (code: 1.0), CS.out.standstill = pcmCruise and hold (code: vEgoRaw == 0), and the 4a reset happens after 100 frames with a vEgo > 0.3 rolling exception (code: 30 frames, no check). The 'REQUESTING window <= 20 frames' starts at lcs = stopping, not at standstill.

The user brief, trap 3, calls bit 29 a capability flag that marks the ESP giving up on hold, and d861e6b ties it to a TSK fault. In route 333 it came on at 7:00, the end of the drive, with no TSK fault. In route 332 it was 0 at the only fault (startup TSK 2->6).

root_causes.hypothesis: H1. No stop announcement to the ESP before the car stops, so the ESP never grants an unlimited standstill. hold_tsk_owned switches to HMS=4 on the first stopping frame below 1.0 m/s. On hill stops the planner lags, so OP's stopping state starts at or after the moment the wheels hit 0 (uphill), or below 1.0 m/s (slow downhill). On those stops ACC_07 never carries Anhalten / HMS=1 / Anhalteweg 0.3, and ESP_21 bit 63 (the ESP's ACC stopping procedure) never runs while the car is moving. Without that procedure the ESP treats the TSK's standstill braking as a time-limited standstill phase. TSK_Status goes to 6 a few seconds into the stop.
root_causes.evidence_for: (1) The replay study shows that the only CAN difference between hold_tsk_owned and its parent is the parent's 0.40 s stop-announcement window. The ACC block md5 is the same on all refs, and frame diffs are limited to [-2.36..-1.98] on flat and [+0.06..+0.44] on +11%. After that window, both send the same frames. (2) Every hold logged without a fault had that window while the car was still moving. Route 333 stop #2: HMS 1 at -2.37 s (v 1.01), bit 63 on at -2.34, HMS 4 at -1.97 (v 0.67), bit 63 off at -1.94; it then held 26.3 s at TSK 3 (stop #1 held 21.1 s). Route 332 at +2.4%: latch 2.10 s before standstill, held about 11 s. (3) Replay: on uphill stops with plan lag (0.04 s and 0.50 s), hold_tsk_owned sends HMS1 for 0.00 s and ACC_07 Anhalten never appears, HMS sequence 0>4>0. Onset-speed sweep: hold_tsk_owned's announcement is 0 frames whenever the stopping state starts at or below 1.01 m/s, so 'any hill' is effectively 'stopping state below 1 m/s'. (4) Route 338: accFaulted at 0:23 with v=0, about 3-4 s after the stop (1.3 m/s at 0:18, 0.5 at 0:19). That fits a short factory standstill limit: the VW wiki says ACC-low cars make the driver take over 'after a very short delay', and a T6.1 owner reports about 3 s. (5) RJ, PR #2764: 'MQB cars without an EPB will fault if the ESP holds the brakes for too long at a standstill' and 'If we transition from stopping to starting before the car has reached a standstill, we can ask for brake indefinitely'. RJ's code sends ACC_07 STOP below 9.5 km/h until bit 63 appears, then latches START. (6) The DBC has ESP_08 bit 14 ESP_Stillstandsphase_erschoepft ('standstill phase exhausted'). (7) The history repeatedly says that holding HMS 4 without a hold request faults (f30a396 'permanent HMS=4 -> SRBM'; 6bacc4d 'HMS=4 accumulates SRBM ... trips TSK'), and the user calls this 'an issue we have had previously'.
root_causes.evidence_against: No CAN trace of the 337/338 faults exists yet, so bit 63, HMS order, Brm and the time from standstill to fault are all unconfirmed. Route 337's stop time is unknown: the last speed event is at 3:13 and the fault at 3:35, so the 'few seconds' figure rests on route 338 alone. On flat stops hold_tsk_owned sends 0-1 HMS1 frames. If one frame does not start bit 63, H1 predicts that long flat stops fault too, and the user reported only hill faults (they may not have noticed, or the flat stops were short). That a short bit-63 episode grants an unlimited standstill comes from RJ and has not been shown on this car. Bit 53 was never seen, so what the ESP does internally is inferred.

It faults after a timeout. This is a variant of H1 in which the trigger is a plausibility/consistency check rather than a standstill timer. The cure is the same: an ACC_07 stop request while the car is still moving.
